title: identity-runtime: governed, reversible avatar personalities with leased capabilities
description:
Research prototype. identity-runtime is classical, deterministic, standard-library-only Python (3.10+) that treats an avatar personality as a versioned identity state rather than a file.

An uploaded personality manifest is checked against a schema, compiled against a runtime-side capability registry (unknown or never-grantable capabilities such as modify_safety_policy are rejected; limits are clamped; mandatory human approval cannot be removed) and screened by a deterministic shadow simulation (text screening for prompt injection and self-escalation, plus fixed adversarial probes replayed against the compiled policy; an optional model hook is off by default). It then waits: identity, reasoning, memory policy and interaction need one human approver, tool and safety policy need two distinct approvers, and the avatar cannot approve itself.

Capabilities are short, revocable leases granted by a person and bound to the active version. Each action request is denied, held for a human, or authorised with a proof object whose hash is written to a hash-chained JSONL ledger that fails closed on tampering, truncation or tail deletion. Committed versions are stored by checksum and can be rolled back; commit and rollback revoke all leases. Optional HMAC-SHA256 approval tokens bind each approval to what is approved.

OES-61440 names a fixed hierarchy of 61,440 threshold channels (1,920 membranes, 480 supervisors, 120 sectors) used as a transparent tripwire. It is deterministic and not learned; its settings are illustrative and uncalibrated, and it is not a safety guarantee.

Limits. Text screening can be bypassed by paraphrase; the runtime executes nothing and provides no sandbox; HMAC tokens are shared-secret, not public-key signatures; the ledger is tamper-evident, not tamper-proof. Example personalities: a fictional educational character inspired by the historical inventor Nikola Tesla (1856-1943), which is not Nikola Tesla and is not affiliated with Tesla, Inc., and Sparky the Beaver, the Fredericton Holograms mascot. 71 tests run in CI on Python 3.10-3.13.
